definitions.explanation: A soft pink color reminiscent of peach blossoms. One of the traditional Japanese color names.
Used figuratively to describe matters related to love, romance, or sexual affairs. Similar to English 'rosy' in the romantic sense.

examples.japanese: {桃色|ももいろ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦リボン→リボン：11256_ribon⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦つけた→つける：00562_tsukeru⟧。
examples.english: I put on a pink ribbon.

examples.japanese: ⟦{空|そら}→空：02216_sora⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧{桃色|ももいろ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{染|そ}まった→染まる：04254_somaru⟧。

examples.english: Many pink flowers bloom in the spring garden.

examples.japanese: {桃色|ももいろ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{噂|うわさ}→噂：01871_uwasa⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{広|ひろ}まった→広まる：02404_hiromaru⟧。
⟦あの→あの：00915_ano⟧⟦{二人|ふたり}→二人：00622_futari⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{桃色|ももいろ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{関係|かんけい}→関係：01298_kankei⟧らしい。
examples.english: Those two apparently have a romantic relationship.

examples.japanese: ⟦{芸能|げいのう}{人|じん}→芸能人：14959_geinoujin⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{桃色|ももいろ}スキャンダル⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦ニュース→ニュース：04437_nyuusu⟧になった。
examples.english: The celebrity's love scandal made the news.

notes:
USAGE:
As a color term, {桃色|ももいろ} is a traditional Japanese color name referring to a soft pink. In modern usage, ⟦ピンク→ピンク：04718_pinku⟧ is more commonly used for the color pink in everyday conversation, while {桃色|ももいろ} retains a more traditional or literary feel.

The figurative sense — romantic or amorous — appears in set phrases like {桃色|ももいろ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{噂|うわさ}→噂：01871_uwasa⟧ (romantic rumor) and {桃色|ももいろ}スキャンダル (love scandal). This usage is somewhat old-fashioned but still understood.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {桃色|ももいろ}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{噂|うわさ}→噂：01871_uwasa⟧: romantic rumor
- {桃色|ももいろ}スキャンダル: love scandal
- {桃色|ももいろ}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{染|そ}まる→染まる：04254_somaru⟧: to turn pink
